channel.title: Neper blog
channel.description: Notes from measuring Neper: memory, WebAssembly, desktop toolchains, text rendering, charts, databases and LLM cost, with the columns where it loses.

item.title: A 1 TiB ceiling that costs 3 MiB
item.description: How a Neper program grows into memory with no flag: an arena reserved, not allocated, and the measured limits on Windows and Linux.

item.title: Neper writes WebAssembly itself
item.description: Neper's own compiler writes wasm32-wasi modules with no LLVM: an 18 KB hello world, a 1.7 MB window and the compiler running in a browser.

item.title: Ten languages, one window: what you install
item.description: One compiler for Windows and Linux desktop programs, nothing to install, a 2.7 MiB window: compared with ten languages install guides.

item.title: Why Neper is built for the agent loop
item.description: Search, generate, edit, check, repair: what each step costs a model and the language rules, JSONL commands and diagnostics that make it cheap.

item.title: ClearType text in Neper
item.description: What subpixel ClearType text costs: measured glyph rendering against native Windows captures, and the trade-offs.

item.title: Faster charts, smaller SVG, and what we are doing about PNG size
item.description: How fast 234 chart types render, and why PNG size and render speed trade off: measured times and file sizes for every chart.

item.title: 234 charts, and when to use each
item.description: A field guide to all 234 charts e.gfx.chart can draw: which question each answers, when to pick it, and speed against matplotlib.

item.title: A million lines, eight compilers
item.description: The sc1m program (1,000 modules, 920,554 lines) in eight compilers: compile and run times with verified output, and where each language lands.

item.title: Six algorithms we first skipped
item.description: A backtracking regex, mixed-integer programming, model checking, crash-dump parsing, Windows and Kerberos sign-on, and AC-2001: one program each.

item.title: Bring your own OpenSSL: SQL Server scans, three times faster
item.description: x.microsoft.tds hands TLS to the host's OpenSSL at run time: SQL Server scans 3.2-3.6x faster, and Neper's scan leads C, Go and Rust.

item.title: One SQL contract, five drivers
item.description: e.db, Neper's SQL contract, and its SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, ODBC and SQL Server drivers: what differs, and one measured workload.

item.title: Neper vs Dart: what it costs an LLM to write each one
item.description: Seven days of Claude transcripts measured byte by byte: what Neper and Dart cost per KB, and where each wins on edits, context and repair.
